question: Which of the following statements are correct? 1. The second item of the Great Sage set collected by the player is the Golden Feng-Tail Crown (凤翅紫金冠). 2. At the end of Chapter 6, there is no animated short similar to those in the previous five chapters. 3. After the player obtains the Lotus Silk Cloudtreaders (藕丝步云履), the character's critical damage is 152%. 4. At the first meditation spot after defeating the Earth Deity of the Flaming Mountains (火焰山), the 'Lingguang' point obtained was chosen to boost critical damage.

rollouts.answer: None of the four statements is correct.

rollouts.failure_point: Statement 4 evaluated at the wrong time window (75090-75150s, ~4900s after the true clue interval 70256-70311s) and statement 2 misjudged as false because a boss-defeat cinematic near the finale was mistaken for the disputed 'animated short'.

db_evidence.notes: The clue interval for statement 4 (70256-70311s) is a real, DB-indexed event (event_steps rows at 70260-70320 describe the 根基/武艺 skill-tree menu right after the Flaming Mountains Earth Deity boss victory at ~70050s), so it was in principle retrievable, but only 1 of 5 rollouts (rollout-03) queried a window close to it (70940-71010s, ~700-900s off); the other four queried an unrelated later meditation/shrine screen around 75000-75330s that also exists in-game but is not the one the question refers to. My own frame extraction inside the true window (70256-70311s) shows the player cycling through several 根基/体段修行 nodes (方圆径寸, 皮肉扭糙, 气息不绝, 威能凶猛); the crit-damage node 威能凶猛 is visible but shown with 0/2 Lingguang points remaining and a red '无法参悟' (cannot select) label when it is reached, which is at least ambiguous evidence against a clean 'yes, crit damage was chosen' reading — so even rollout-03's 'correct' answer for statement 4 may be right only by chance/partial-credit judging rather than an accurate read of the true evidence. For statement 2, the clue window (84526-84595s) is the game's true final ending: a boss-defeat cinematic (84270-84450s) followed immediately by full production end-credits (84540-84912s per event_steps), not a chapter-style animated short — all 5 rollouts instead pointed at a nearby boss-defeat/CG cutscene (82110-84400s range, varying per rollout) and concluded an animated short exists, missing the intended contrast with the previous chapters' distinct animated-short convention.

root_causes: Systematic statement-2 error across all 5/5 rollouts: agents found some cinematic/CG footage near the chapter/game ending and equated it with 'an animated short similar to previous chapters', without checking the specific stylistic/format distinction the question demands (a standalone animated short vs. an in-engine boss-defeat cutscene followed by credits).

Wrong time-window retrieval for statement 4 in 3/5 rollouts (0, 2, 4): they queried a 'first meditation/shrine spot' around 75000-75330s that is a different, later menu screen than the true clue interval (70256-70311s), likely because semantic_search/run_sql surfaced a nearby but incorrect 'rest spot after boss fight' event instead of the one immediately following the Earth Deity victory.

Even the rollout that did query near the correct window (rollout-03, 70940-71010s) was still off by 700-900s from the true clue interval, and my own frame check of the true window shows the crit-damage node was browsed with 0 Lingguang points remaining, casting some doubt on whether 'critical damage was chosen' is unambiguously true from the raw footage.

Score differences (0 vs 3) among the 5 rollouts stem entirely from whether statement 4 was assessed as correct (matching reference {2,4}); getting statement 2 right was never achieved by any rollout, capping the maximum observed score at partial credit (3/5) rather than a full match.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly identified statement 1 as false (凤翅紫金冠 is the first, not second, item) via a well-targeted clip_qa(77580-77610/77640) call.
All 5 rollouts correctly identified statement 3 as false (154% not 152% critical damage) via a well-targeted clip_qa(~79500-79560) call.

The tool pipeline (read_skill -> semantic_search -> run_sql -> clip_qa -> submit_answer) consistently converged on the same correct visual answers for statements 1 and 3 across all 5 independent rollouts, showing the retrieval-to-clip_qa handoff works when the target event is well-anchored (chest-opening popup, stat screen) and near the given clue timestamps.
transferable_lessons: For 'first X after event Y' style questions, verify the retrieved timestamp is anchored immediately adjacent to event Y's own timestamp (e.g. right after a boss-victory message) rather than trusting a generic semantic-search hit for 'meditation/shrine screen' that may return a later, unrelated instance of the same UI.

When a clip_qa sub-agent reports a resource counter (e.g. 'N/M' points), treat a red/disabled state (e.g. '无法参悟', 0 points remaining) as evidence AGAINST a selection actually being made, not as neutral texture — the agent should ask clip_qa explicitly whether the highlighted node was confirmed/spent, not just previewed/hovered.

For 'no animated short/cutscene' negative-existence statements, don't equate any cinematic-looking footage with the specific referent named in the question; compare its format against the previous instances (query similar events at the corresponding point in earlier chapters) before concluding a match.

When multiple clue_intervals are given for one question, deliberately search a window centered on each given clue_interval start/end rather than letting semantic_search's coarse hit pick a nearby-but-different occurrence of the same UI pattern.
open_questions: Whether the reference answer's claim for statement 4 (Lingguang point spent on critical damage) is itself fully correct — my own frame inspection of the true clue window (70256-70311s) shows the crit-damage node ('威能凶猛') displayed with 0/2 points remaining ('无法参悟') when reached, which is at least ambiguous against a clean 'yes it was chosen' reading; this would need the raw video reviewed second-by-second (not just 2-8s stepped frames) to resolve conclusively.

Whether the game's true final chapter (ending in full credits at 84540-84912s) is indeed labeled 'Chapter 6' by the game itself, which would confirm the reference's framing of statement 2; not independently verified beyond the DB descriptions.
